chunks: Al-Nadr (ibn Suwayd) from Yahya al-Halabi from Ayyub who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, the moment when your enemy will have the most intense hatred for this matter will be when the soul reaches here,' and he gestured towards his throat.

Then he said: 'There was a man from the family of Uthman who would often curse Ali (peace be upon him), so one of his maid servants who would visit us told me about that. She said, “When he was about to die, he said, “What do I have to do with them?!””'
I said [to the Imam (peace be upon him)], “May Allah make me your ransom! Why did he say this?”
He said, “[It was] when he was shown some of the punishment [that awaits him for rejecting the wilayah].”

Have you not heard the verse wherein Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: But no, by your Lord, they will never be [true] believers until they accept your judgement in all their disputes, and find no resistance within themselves against your decision and submit wholeheartedly (Q4:65)?
Far be it! Far be it! No, by Allah [it will not be so] until this thing is well established in the heart, even if he prays and fasts.’”

key_terms.آل عُثْمَان: The family of Uthman ibn Affan
key_terms.فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ: In what caused dispute between them

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the moment of death in Shia theology regarding the acceptance of divine authority?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the concept of *khulus* (sincerity) by contrasting superficial ritual observance with deep-seated conviction, using the deathbed realization of a man from the Umayyad family as a case study. The Imam emphasizes that true acceptance of divine authority requires the heart to be free of residual resentment, a state often lacking in political opponents of the Ahl al-Bayt even if they pray and fast. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly distinction between outward submission (*islam*) and inward faith (*iman*), particularly regarding the love for the Imams.
